lines.text: a graph is not a diagram — it is a set of relationships
graph theory begins when you stop asking "which route should I try?" and ask "what does the structure allow at …
Watch a tangled graph draw itself. Springs pull linked nodes together while repulsion pushes every pair apart
pathfinding does not move through space — it moves through a graph that happens to be embedded in space
a rhizome has no beginning and no end — only middles
Read a network as hierarchy, community, and circulation at once
maximum flow through a network equals the minimum cut that separates source from sink
Topological sort — linear ordering of vertices in a directed acyclic graph
a strongly connected component is a pocket of mutual reachability
Kosaraju's algorithm proves that strongly connected components are the same in a graph and its transpose
the minimum spanning tree is the cheapest way to keep everyone connected
Karger's algorithm is a bet that randomness repeated enough times becomes certainty
push-relabel proves that maximum flow can be found without ever finding a complete path
matching is the mathematics of pairing — who connects with whom
